scope: 1960 teachers-union dispute: split cabinet/ministry/labor actors and administrative actions

findings.claim: On 1960-06-23 Education Minister Lee Byeong-do publicly called for dissolution of teachers unions and threatened coercive measures against continued organization or membership; union representatives countered with a written rebuttal and resignation recommendation.
findings.caution: The chronology is an archival chronology citing contemporary Chosun Ilbo and Dong-A Ilbo; underlying newspaper pages and ministry records remain primary targets.

findings.claim: On 1960-05-07 Lee announced an education-policy response to post-April-Revolution campus rejection movements: students should avoid political involvement, educators should sever party ties, and a provisional Education Countermeasures Committee would be formed to pursue education-policy and legal reform.

The Education vice-minister publicly stated on 1960-05-09 that the ministry would neither block nor encourage formation of teachers unions; on 1960-07-01 he publicly explained the ministry's suspension of Kyungpook National University medical school after a professor-abduction/confinement incident.
sources: Korea Democracy Foundation Dictionary, 교원노조결성운동, https://dict.kdemo.or.kr/entry/94/
findings.caution: The May 9 statement is presently verified through the Foundation's synthesized dictionary entry; recover the cited contemporary press or ministry record.

findings.claim: As Health and Social Affairs vice-minister, Kim stated on 1960-06-18 that authorities would recognize unions upon notification; this position conflicted with the Education Ministry's anti-union line and preceded the Health and Social Affairs Ministry's June 22 request for a Justice Ministry legal interpretation.
findings.source: Korea Democracy Foundation Dictionary, 교원노조결성운동, https://dict.kdemo.or.kr/entry/94/
findings.caution: Exact wording, delegation of authority, and the June 22 inter-ministerial request require underlying ministry/press documents.

findings.claim: On 1960-06-29 the labor body formally accused Education Minister Lee Byeong-do of violating the Labor Union Act over interference with teachers' union organization and threatened employment disadvantages.
findings.caution: Recover the complaint itself, receiving prosecutor's-office record, and any disposition before asserting legal outcome.

adversarial_checks: Do not model the teachers-union dispute as a single Lee Byeong-do decision; Education, Health/Social Affairs, Justice, labor organizations and teacher organizations held distinguishable roles.
Do not equate a public statement with a written administrative order.
Do not infer the Justice Ministry's legal conclusion merely from the fact that Health/Social Affairs requested an interpretation.
Do not infer that the June 29 criminal complaint produced prosecution or conviction without disposition records.
Do not infer presidential direction from cabinet/ministry conduct during the transitional government without presidential/cabinet records.
Do not collapse public-school and private-school legal theories; the archival synthesis identifies different statutory arguments.
Do not infer that Lee Hang-nyeong's May 9 neutrality statement remained ministry policy after later June actions.
Do not infer that Kim Hak-muk personally authored the June 22 request to Justice; the current source attributes that action to the ministry.
Do not treat later biographical career summaries as proof of exact appointment dates where appointment instruments are available.
Do not merge the July 1 Kyungpook National University suspension with the teachers-union dispute; connect through education-administration actors only.
